final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor introduced no new admissible evidence and mainly narrowed the claim to a caveated position based on the same record. That reinterpretation is directionally more careful, but it does not close the initial concerns. The policy text requires current release documentation to reflect current evaluation results and to disclose material segment weaknesses or cover them with approved mitigation. Admissible evidence still shows a current small-business onboarding regression, no attached disclosure language, no approved mitigation or risk acceptance, and only an informal monitoring comment. Aggregate readiness and lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents support general launch readiness, but they do not satisfy the model-card disclosure predicate. A caveat can support compliant_with_caveats only when the caveat describes a condition already evidenced or otherwise satisfied within the record; here, the proposed caveat depends on disclosure that is not itself in evidence, so the unresolved compliance predicate remains.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the current release documentation reflects the current evaluation results after the retrieval configuration change.
No admissible evidence shows the small-business onboarding regression is explicitly disclosed as a material limitation for the named launch use case.
No admissible evidence shows an approved mitigation or risk acceptance covering the current subgroup regression before launch.
The record still contains only an informal post-launch monitoring comment, which does not satisfy the policy predicate.
Prior approval of the same model family remains stale context and does not satisfy the current-release certification requirement.
